polaris: LP29-C2: graph metrics are viable only if global organization (lambda_2, rho_A, high-betweenness attack loss) predicts external residual labels after Srivastava-style orbital-overlap and controls; otherwise they are overlap reparameterizations.

independence_guardrail.namespace_rule: All Round 2 B artifacts use current/B paths and B-C2-R2 identifiers. No current/A files or A Round 2 outputs are inputs.

framework: Distributed network reliability / error-correcting redundancy under a fixed local capacity budget.
findings: Round 2 converts the B route into a leakage-controlled protocol. The graph convention is now locked; residualization is train-fold only; baseline and graph namespaces are separated; synthetic benchmarks are admitted only as software sanity checks. The live B claim is conditional: global graph organization is independent only if it has held-out residual power on external material labels after OI and nuisance controls.

graph_convention_lock.w_ij_definition: w_ij = max(0, OI_ij / OI_ref) for an edge i-j passing the predeclared structural/orbital cutoff. OI_ref is fixed inside the provenance table before any labels are read.
graph_convention_lock.nonnegativity: A_w[i,j] = A_w[j,i] = w_ij >= 0; A_w[i,i] = 0. Negative hopping signs, phases, or antibonding information are not encoded in this graph layer.
graph_convention_lock.degree: d_i = sum_j A_w[i,j]. Isolated nodes are allowed; they force lambda_2 = 0 if the graph is disconnected.
graph_convention_lock.laplacian_primary: Use symmetric normalized weighted Laplacian L_sym = I - D^{-1/2} A_w D^{-1/2}. The primary lambda_2 is the second-smallest eigenvalue of L_sym and is dimensionless in [0,2].
graph_convention_lock.laplacian_secondary: Unnormalized L_w = D - A_w may be reported only as a sensitivity analysis with units equal to w_ij. It cannot be mixed with L_sym coefficients.
graph_convention_lock.rho_A_definition: rho_A = spectral_radius(A_w / S_w), where S_w = sum_{i<j} w_ij. This makes rho_A dimensionless and budget-normalized.
graph_convention_lock.rho_A_direction: At fixed OI budget, controls, and graph-mode localization, larger rho_A is expected to align with a stronger coherent backbone mode and better mobility/Drude/Wannier good-label residuals. If the top eigenvector participation ratio is low, rho_A is treated as hub/localization risk rather than a positive transport sign.
graph_convention_lock.attack_damage_definition: D_metric(E_remove) = max(0, metric_before - metric_after) / max(metric_before, epsilon). attack_gap = D_high_betweenness - mean(D_random_matched).
graph_convention_lock.attack_direction: Positive attack_gap means high-betweenness removal is more destructive than matched random removal; larger attack_gap predicts worse good-label residuals and worse bad-label residuals after baseline controls.

residual_protocol_choice.allowed_model_1_raw_label: Fit y_external ~ B_baseline + G_graph with nested cross-validation. Compare against y_external ~ B_baseline.
residual_protocol_choice.allowed_model_2_residual_only: Inside each training fold, fit baseline y_external ~ B_baseline, transform train/test labels into residuals with the train-fitted baseline, residualize each graph feature against B_baseline using train-fitted regressions, then fit r_y ~ r_G.
residual_protocol_choice.forbidden_mixture: Do not fit y_residual ~ controls + OI + graph. Once labels are residualized, baseline controls and OI are not placed again on the RHS.
residual_protocol_choice.selected_for_C2_round2: residual_only is the primary B protocol because it directly tests the post-OI graph signal. raw_label is retained as a robustness mirror.

baseline_namespace.rule: Baseline terms are computed without graph spectral operations and without target-adjacent labels.

graph_namespace.rule: Graph terms are structure-only functions of A_w and its allowed null transformations. They never include external labels or target-derived quantities.

forbidden_controls: measured Hall factor from same experiment
conductivity-derived mean free path using the target mobility
carrier density inferred by inverting the same target if not independently measured
Drude fit residuals from the same spectrum
plasma frequency algebraically used to define the target
scattering time derived from the target label
band velocity or curvature computed from the same target band if it defines the label
Wannier hopping summary used directly as the target
graph Hamiltonian eigenvalue labels from the same A_w
line fit quality metrics from the same linewidth target
IPR computed from the same graph proxy eigenvectors
batch labels that encode target measurement settings

train_fold_residualization_pseudocode: split samples into outer folds with batch/family blocking
for each outer fold: train_idx, test_idx = split
fit baseline_model_y on train_idx using only B0_* columns
for each G1_* feature: fit baseline_model_g on train_idx using only B0_* columns
compare against intercept-only residual model and against batch-preserving permutations
never refit residualizers on train+test jointly

layer_1.mathematical_core: Reliability is not fixed by total link capacity; it depends on expansion, cut structure, and targeted-failure response.
layer_1.LP29_mapping: S_w/OI_norm is total local capacity; lambda_2 is expansion; attack_gap is targeted bridge vulnerability.
layer_1.testable_prediction: At matched B0_OI_norm and weight histogram, a high-lambda_2 sample should keep better external good-label residuals than a bottlenecked sample.

layer_2.mathematical_core: Two graphs with equal degree/weight distributions can have different min-cut structure and therefore different all-terminal reliability.
layer_2.LP29_mapping: Amorphous In-s/O-mediated backbones with equal overlap budget can differ in whether current-like paths are distributed or forced through high-betweenness bridges.
layer_2.testable_prediction: High-betweenness defect placement should damage Drude/Hall/Wannier residual labels more than matched random placement if global organization is real.

layer_1.mathematical_core: A code's protection depends on distance and syndrome separability, not only the number of physical bits or checks.
layer_1.LP29_mapping: OI budget is the number/strength of local checks; lambda_2 and attack_gap approximate whether electronic amplitude has redundant alternate routes.
layer_1.testable_prediction: A structure with redundant moderate overlaps can outperform a structure with a few strong bridge overlaps after B0 controls.

layer_2.mathematical_core: Expansion can create a threshold where many small local failures remain correctable, while clustered bridge failures cause abrupt decoding failure.
layer_2.LP29_mapping: If the conductive backbone is expander-like, random local disorder should have weak residual effect; if it is bridge-dominated, targeted high-betweenness disorder should produce a sharp residual drop.
layer_2.testable_prediction: The slope of external good-label residual versus attack_gap should be more negative in bottlenecked families than in high-lambda_2 families, under leave-one-family-out validation.

synthetic_benchmark_gate.purpose: Protocol and software sanity only. It can test whether the pipeline detects a planted graph residual and rejects an OI-only null.
synthetic_benchmark_gate.hard_gate: Any row with synthetic_label_flag=true is excluded from material-claim tables, figures, and conclusions.
minimum_expected_behavior: B-positive synthetic labels show graph residual signal after train-fold residualization.
A-null synthetic labels do not show stable graph residual signal.
Leakage-trap labels are detected as forbidden and never counted as material validation.

strangest_prediction: At fixed nonnegative dimensionless OI capacity budget, a sparse set of defects on high-betweenness backbone edges should reduce external Hall/Drude/Wannier good-label residuals more than a larger random defect set with the same deleted weight.
a_objection: Even with normalized conventions, lambda_2, rho_A, and attack_gap are functions of overlap-derived A_w and may only be nonlinear OI features.
b_response: Correct. B survives only if train-fold residualized G1_* features improve held-out external residual labels beyond B0_* controls and null rewiring/permutation controls. Synthetic success is not evidence for materials.

failed_jumps.reason: Eigenmode analogy did not generate a leakage-controlled external residual protocol.
Load-path intuition collapsed into the same network reliability attack-gap test.

next_plan: Run C2_residual_benchmark.py as a synthetic protocol sanity check, then assemble a same-sample external-label join table with provenance before making any material claim.

claims.statement: With w_ij fixed as nonnegative dimensionless overlap capacity and lambda_2 fixed to L_sym, the graph protocol has comparable units across runs.
assumptions: A_w is symmetric, nonnegative, and label-blind.

claims.statement: The decisive B model is residual-only or raw-label, never a mixed residual-plus-baseline regression.

claims.statement: The deeper isomorphism is error-correcting redundancy: OI controls local capacity, while expansion and attack-gap test whether capacity is globally redundant.
assumptions: Targeted and random attacks are matched by deleted weight or edge count.
Material inference requires external labels and same-sample provenance.

attack_gap residual: negative for good labels and positive for bad labels.
